bestCustomers.name: Third Bracket — HR / Recruitment / Talent Solutions
bestCustomers.whyBoughtThen: The likely trigger was the need to expand organic visibility beyond traditional Google search and establish Third Bracket as an authoritative company that can surface in AI-generated answers when businesses search for recruitment and talent partners.
bestCustomers.whyGoodCustomer:
Third Bracket operates in a search- and reputation-driven professional-services category where potential customers research recruitment and talent partners before engaging. Visibility in Google as well as ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and AI-generated recommendations can directly influence whether the company enters a buyer's consideration set.

Their service category also creates many high-intent discovery opportunities around recruitment companies, hiring partners, executive search, staffing and talent solutions.

bestCustomers.name: Zyngg — Consumer Technology / Mobile App
bestCustomers.whyBoughtThen: The likely trigger was the need to build visibility and digital authority for a growing product rather than depending entirely on paid acquisition or conventional search. Establishing the brand early across Google and AI discovery channels can help create longer-term organic visibility.
bestCustomers.whyGoodCustomer:
Zyngg is a digital-first product where online discovery, brand awareness and category visibility are important for growth. As a technology/app business, its prospective users and partners are naturally more likely to use digital and AI-powered discovery channels.

AEO/GEO can help establish the brand's entity, product positioning, use cases and category relevance across search engines and AI platforms.

bestCustomers.name: Virama Farm Stay — Hospitality / Farm Stay / Travel
bestCustomers.whyBoughtThen: The objective was to increase direct organic discovery for high-intent farm-stay searches and reduce dependence on intermediaries/booking platforms. Virama actively promotes direct WhatsApp/phone booking without platform fees, making increased Google and AI visibility commercially valuable because discovery can translate directly into bookings.
bestCustomers.whyGoodCustomer:
Virama is an excellent AEO/GEO use case because customers actively search questions such as “best farm stay near Bangalore,” “farm stay near Bangalore with pool,” “private farm stay near Bangalore,” “pet-friendly farm stay near Bangalore” and similar recommendation queries.

Virama is a private 3-acre farm stay in Magadi, around 45 km from Bangalore, accommodating up to 28 guests with a private 24-hour pool, bonfire, activities and direct booking. These clear attributes provide substantial structured information that can be optimized for both conventional search and AI answers.

businessTwinRawAnswers.costOfInaction:
As buyers increasingly use AI systems during research and vendor discovery, brands that are absent from AI-generated answers risk becoming invisible during an important part of the buying journey.

Competitors can become the brands repeatedly recommended by AI while the company receives fewer mentions and fewer opportunities to enter buyer consideration.

A company may continue investing heavily in SEO and content while failing to capture visibility in AI-driven discovery.

The longer competitors accumulate authoritative content, citations and machine-readable signals, the harder it can become to close the visibility gap.
businessTwinRawAnswers.problemsSolved:
Companies may rank on Google but remain invisible when prospective customers ask ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini or Google AI Overviews for recommendations, comparisons or solutions.

Their website content may not be structured in a way that AI systems can easily understand, extract and cite. Competitors can therefore appear in AI-generated recommendations even when the company has stronger products, experience or traditional SEO rankings.

DigiPuush solves:

AI search invisibility; lack of brand citations in LLM answers; competitors being recommended instead; poor content structure for AI extraction; weak entity/brand authority; insufficient structured data/schema; declining effectiveness of traditional SEO alone; and lack of visibility into how the brand appears across AI answer engines.

DigiPuush approaches SEO + AEO + GEO as one integrated search strategy, rather than treating AI visibility as an isolated add-on.

The service focuses specifically on measurable visibility across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Google AI Overviews and traditional Google Search.

Key differentiators include AI visibility audits, content restructuring for answer extraction, schema implementation, citation-oriented content, traditional SEO foundations, authority building and ongoing AI citation monitoring.

DigiPuush is also positioned specifically around the Indian market rather than as a generic international GEO consultancy.
businessTwinRawAnswers.typicalCustomerProfile:
B2B SaaS, technology companies, professional services, education, healthcare, financial services, e-commerce and other businesses where customers research providers online before making a purchase.

Ideal companies already invest in their website, content, SEO or digital marketing but have limited visibility when potential customers ask AI platforms for recommendations.

The strongest customers operate in competitive categories where appearing in "best company", "best software", "alternative to", "which provider", comparison and high-intent informational queries can influence purchasing decisions.

Companies with established websites, existing content and some domain authority are particularly attractive because DigiPuush can build on those assets rather than starting from zero.

DigiPuush's current site explicitly says it works with B2B, SaaS and e-commerce brands and shows case-study patterns across B2B SaaS, D2C e-commerce and local services.

bestCustomers.whyBoughtThen: As the platform and enterprise relationships grew, security requirements increased. 24/7 monitoring provided continuous security oversight and threat investigation without requiring a complete internal SOC.
bestCustomers.whyGoodCustomer: Operates a cloud-based AI platform handling sensitive financial, legal and investment information for financial institutions. Enterprise financial customers, sensitive data and security/compliance requirements make continuous monitoring particularly important.

bestCustomers.name: Altoura — Enterprise SaaS / AI Technology
bestCustomers.whyBoughtThen: Growth in enterprise deployments increased the importance of continuous security monitoring and meeting customer security expectations. Outsourced SOC monitoring provided round-the-clock coverage without building a dedicated internal 24/7 SOC.
bestCustomers.whyGoodCustomer: Operates an enterprise cloud platform used by large organizations. Its cloud infrastructure, enterprise customer base, Microsoft-oriented technology environment and security/compliance requirements make it suitable for Aadit's Managed SOC.

bestCustomers.name: Aditi Consulting — Digital Engineering / IT Services
bestCustomers.whyBoughtThen: Increasing infrastructure, workforce and enterprise-client security requirements created a need for dedicated 24/7 security oversight. Aadit's Managed SOC provided continuous monitoring and investigation without the complexity of expanding an internal round-the-clock SOC.
bestCustomers.whyGoodCustomer: A large technology services organization with 2,000+ employees, distributed operations, substantial cloud/IT infrastructure and major enterprise customers. Its scale and infrastructure complexity create a strong requirement for continuous security monitoring.

businessTwinRawAnswers.costOfInaction:
Without continuous security monitoring, suspicious activity can remain undetected for hours or days, allowing attackers more time to compromise accounts, move across systems, steal information or deploy ransomware.

A successful security incident can result in business downtime, data loss, financial losses, customer impact, regulatory exposure, failed security audits and reputational damage.

Companies may also lose or delay enterprise contracts when they cannot demonstrate adequate security monitoring and incident-response capabilities.

Building an equivalent 24/7 internal SOC requires recruiting and retaining multiple cybersecurity professionals, implementing processes and maintaining round-the-clock coverage, making it expensive and operationally difficult for many mid-market organizations.
businessTwinRawAnswers.problemsSolved:
Organizations often have multiple cybersecurity tools generating large volumes of alerts but lack dedicated security analysts to continuously review and investigate them.

Internal IT teams are typically focused on infrastructure and business operations and cannot monitor security events 24/7. This creates gaps during nights, weekends and holidays and increases the possibility of critical alerts being missed.

Aadit's Managed SOC solves:

24/7 security monitoring gaps; shortage of skilled cybersecurity analysts; excessive security alerts and alert fatigue; slow threat detection and investigation; lack of centralized visibility across cloud, endpoints, identities and networks; limited internal incident-response capability; and security monitoring requirements arising from ISO 27001, SOC 2, customer security assessments and other compliance obligations.
businessTwinRawAnswers.dealSizeHistory:
Managed SOC engagements are generally recurring annual contracts, with value increasing according to the number of users/endpoints, infrastructure complexity, cloud workloads, monitoring scope and additional security services required.

Typical target contract value is approximately $30,000–$60,000 annually, with ~$45,000 representing a useful target deal size. Larger organizations and expanded monitoring scopes can result in higher contract values.

Expansion can occur as customers add employees, endpoints, cloud workloads, locations or additional cybersecurity/compliance services.
businessTwinRawAnswers.currentCustomers: Current Managed SOC customers include technology, AI/SaaS and digital engineering companies operating cloud-based environments and serving enterprise customers. Examples include Alphastream.ai, Altoura and Aditi Consulting. These organizations depend heavily on technology infrastructure, handle sensitive business/customer data, and require strong security monitoring. Customers range from growing technology companies to large global organizations, demonstrating that the service can support different levels of infrastructure complexity.
businessTwinRawAnswers.objectionHistory:
Common objections include:

“We already have security tools in place.”
“Our internal IT/security team monitors this.”
“We don't need 24/7 monitoring yet.”
“We haven't had a major security incident.”
“Our current MSP already handles security.”
“The budget is too high.”
“We are comparing other MDR/MSSP providers.”
“We can build this capability internally.”
“We don't generate enough security alerts to justify a SOC.”
“We can revisit this during the next budget cycle.”

Other delays occur because of procurement, vendor onboarding, management approval or uncertainty about the immediate ROI of security monitoring.
businessTwinRawAnswers.wonOpportunities:
Won opportunities typically involve companies with established IT/cloud environments but without sufficient internal resources for true 24/7 security monitoring. Common characteristics include cloud adoption, Microsoft-centric environments, distributed users, enterprise customers, sensitive data, growing security complexity and compliance requirements.

Deals become stronger when there is a clear trigger: an upcoming ISO 27001/SOC 2 or customer audit, enterprise customer security requirements, a recent security concern, rapid growth, increasing endpoints/cloud workloads, or management realizing that the existing IT team cannot effectively monitor security around the clock.

Aadit wins when customers value human-led 24/7 monitoring, manual investigation of alerts, direct access to experienced analysts, flexibility and cost-effectiveness compared with building an internal SOC.
businessTwinRawAnswers.competitorHistory:
Managed SOC/MSSP/MDR providers, regional cybersecurity service providers, Microsoft security partners, and customers' incumbent MSPs.

The most common competitive alternatives are often not another SOC provider, but the customer's existing internal IT/security team, automated security tools, an existing MSP providing basic security monitoring, or the customer considering building an internal SOC.

Where formal vendor comparisons occur, alternatives may include providers such as Arctic Wolf, Sophos MDR, Rapid7 MDR, eSentire, Secureworks and similar managed security providers.
businessTwinRawAnswers.expansionPatterns:
Customers can initially engage Aadit for 24/7 security monitoring and subsequently expand the relationship as their infrastructure, employee base and security requirements grow. Expansion opportunities include adding more endpoints, cloud workloads, business units or geographic locations to SOC coverage; vulnerability assessment and penetration testing (VAPT); ISO 27001 and SOC 2 readiness; security assessments; incident response; cloud security; endpoint and identity security; and broader managed IT/security services.

Growth, acquisitions, new offices, cloud migrations, compliance initiatives, major enterprise customers and increased employee counts can all create natural opportunities to expand the engagement.
businessTwinRawAnswers.lostOpportunities:
Opportunities are more likely to be lost or delayed when cybersecurity monitoring is viewed as non-urgent, there is no immediate compliance/customer requirement, management believes existing security tools are sufficient, or the internal IT team believes it can continue handling security monitoring.

Other common barriers include budget constraints, comparison with lower-cost automated MDR/MSSP offerings, preference for an incumbent IT/security provider, long procurement processes and organizations deciding to postpone the project.
businessTwinRawAnswers.salesCycleHistory:
Typical Managed SOC opportunities can take approximately 30–90 days from qualified opportunity to closure.

Sales cycles tend to be considerably shorter when there is a strong buying trigger such as an upcoming audit, enterprise customer security requirement, security incident, compliance deadline or immediate requirement for 24/7 monitoring.

Sales cycles become longer when the requirement is exploratory, there is no defined security deadline, multiple stakeholders are involved, budget approval is pending, or the customer is comparing an outsourced SOC against building capabilities internally.

businessTwinRawAnswers.typicalSalesCycle: 30–90 days; can shorten to 2–4 weeks when there is an active security incident, audit deadline, compliance requirement or enterprise customer security demand.

context.offeringDescription:
Aadit provides a fully managed 24/7 Security Operations Center (SOC) for organizations that need continuous cybersecurity monitoring without the cost and complexity of building an internal SOC.

Aadit's security analysts continuously monitor the customer's IT and cloud environment, investigate security alerts, identify genuine threats, prioritize incidents, and coordinate with the customer's IT team for response and remediation.

The service provides continuous human security oversight across endpoints, identities, cloud infrastructure, networks and security systems, helping organizations detect and respond to threats before they become serious security incidents.
